question: On ultrasound, a non-compressible appendix measuring 6 mm or more in outer diameter with periappendiceal echogenic fat is diagnostic of acute appendicitis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The ultrasound criterion for appendicitis is a non-compressible appendix ≥6 mm outer diameter with periappendiceal echogenic fat. Below 6 mm and compressible, appendicitis is unlikely. This is the single most important ultrasound measurement to remember for appendicitis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The threshold of ≥6 mm outer diameter in a non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure in the right iliac fossa, with surrounding echogenic fat (periappendiceal inflammation), is the established ultrasound criterion for appendicitis. Colour Doppler showing hyperaemia adds specificity. A normal-appearing compressible appendix <6 mm effectively excludes appendicitis.
